Objective

A returning player should land back in the existing Sign-Up queue, not create a duplicate record.

Implementation Requirements

* When a new Study Link Click arrives for an existing Archived Sign-Up, and the click occurs AFTER a defined grace period has elapsed since archival, reactivate the Sign-Up instead of creating a new one

* Grace period stored in a CUSTOM SETTING so admins can change it without editing automation. Set to 2 days for now

* Archived Sign-Up is defined as Status = Archived AND not flagged for fraud

* Auto-reactivation applies ONLY when the click matches an existing Sign-Up on BOTH Player AND Deal. No match -> create a new Sign-Up as normal

Acceptance Criteria

* Click inside the grace period does not reactivate

* Click outside the grace period reactivates and clears archive reasons

* Fraud-flagged archived Sign-Ups are skipped

* Non-matching clicks still create new Sign-Ups

BUILD-04 (production Study Link Click resolution flow). This is a NEW BRANCH of that flow, not a standalone automation. Do NOT build a second record-triggered flow on Study Link Click — scope it into BUILD-04. See the pinned note on BUILD-04.

=== OBJECTIVE ===

Add two read-only formula fields on Deal__c that derive short codes from the existing Market Country / Market State picklists (which hold full names). These are the reusable building blocks for the Market display field, list views, reporting groupings and any outbound CMS payload that needs a code rather than a full name.

Reps continue to maintain Market_Country\__c and Market_State_\_c only. Neither new field is editable.

=== WHY FORMULA, NOT A MAPPING TABLE ===

Custom Metadata Types were evaluated and rejected: formula fields can only reference $CustomMetadata with a STATIC record name, so there is no dynamic lookup from a field value. A CMT approach would require Flow or Apex, which is over-engineered for a display/derivation string. Hardcoded CASE is the correct pattern here.

Note for future reference: renaming the picklist API values to codes (label stays the full name) would remove the need for the state CASE entirely, since TEXT() returns the API value. Rejected for now because the CMS integration and data migration mappings write the full names, and changing API values pre-go-live would ripple into those. Revisit if the codes are ever needed in more places.

=== FIELD 1: Market Country Code ===

API Name: Market_Country_Code__c

Label: Market Country Code

Type: Formula (Text)

Blank handling: Treat blank fields as Blanks

* Market Country = Canada -> CA

* Market Country = United States & Canada -> US & CA

* Market Country = blank -> blank

=== OBJECTIVE ===

Rebuild the two Deal label formulas to read Operator - Market - Vertical using the new market short-code fields, and collapse separators when a segment is blank.

Two changes from the previous format:

1\. Partner is REMOVED from the label (intentional - see Decisions below).

2\. Market is rendered from the short-code fields (ON · CA) instead of the full picklist names (Canada Ontario).

=== DEFECT BEING FIXED ===

Both original formulas referenced Partner__r.Name and the market picklists WITHOUT blank guards. Any Deal with no Partner rendered a double separator and an orphaned space, e.g.:

Bet99 - - Canada Ontario - Casino

The new formulas guard every optional segment.

=== FIELD 1: Deal_Name__c (Formula, Text) ===

Original:

Operator__r.Name

& IF(ISBLANK(Partner__c), "",

" - " & Partner__r.Name)

& IF(TEXT(Market_Country__c) = "", "",

" - " & TEXT(Market_Country__c) &

IF(TEXT(Market_State\__c) = "", "", " " & TEXT(Market_State_\_c)))

& IF(TEXT(Vertical__c) = "", "",

" - " & TEXT(Vertical__c))

New:

Operator__r.Name

& IF(ISBLANK(Market_Country_Code__c), "",

" - " & IF(Market_State_Code__c = "Multi-state",

Market_Country_Code__c & " · Multi-state",

Market_State_Code\__c & " · " & Market_Country_Code_\_c))

& IF(ISPICKVAL(Vertical\__c, ""), "", " - " & TEXT(Vertical_\_c))

=== FIELD 2: Deal__c (Formula, Text - hyperlink) ===

Original:

HYPERLINK( "/" & Id, Operator\__r.Name & " - " & Partnerr.Name & " - " & TEXT(Market_Countryc) & " " & TEXT(Market_Statec) & " - " & TEXT(Vertical_\_c), "\_self" )

New:

HYPERLINK("/" & Id, Deal_Name__c, "\_self")

This references Deal_Name__c rather than duplicating the logic, so the plain-text label and the hyperlink label can never drift. Confirmed to compile.

=== EXPECTED OUTPUT ===

Operator | Market Country | Market State | Vertical | Deal Name

Bet99 | Canada | Ontario | Casino | Bet99 - ON · CA - Casino

Bet99 | United States | Ohio | Sports | Bet99 - OH · US - Sports

Bet99 | United States | (blank) | Sports | Bet99 - US · Multi-state - Sports

Bet99 | (blank) | (blank) | Casino | Bet99 - Casino

=== COMPILED-SIZE CONSTRAINT (important for anyone editing these) ===

The first attempt had Deal_Name\__c reference Market_Displayc, which in turn references Market_State_Code_\_c (a 69-branch CASE). Salesforce inlines referenced formula fields into one compiled expression, and this failed:

"Compiled formula is too big to execute (20,367 characters). Maximum size is 15,000 characters."

Resolved by having Deal_Name\__c reference Market_State_Codec / Market_Country_Code_\_c DIRECTLY and drop the flag emoji, which removed a nesting layer and brought it under 15,000.

Consequence: there is limited headroom left. Do NOT add further nested formula references to Deal_Name\__c or Dealc without re-running Check Syntax. If more headroom is ever needed, the fix is to sever the chain - either convert Market_State_Code_\_c to a Text field populated by a before-save Flow, or rename the Market State picklist API values to the 2-letter codes so the 69-branch CASE disappears entirely.

=== DECISIONS ===

* Partner removed from the Deal label. Deliberate. Note the side effect: partner deals and Direct deals are no longer distinguishable by name alone, so reporting and list views must surface Partner as its own column. If this needs reversing, insert after Operator__r.Name:

& IF(ISBLANK(Partner\__c), "", " - " & Partner_\_r.Name)

* Flag emoji excluded from both label fields. The emoji lives only in the UI display field (BUILD-118). Keeps Deal Name clean for CSV export, email templates and any outbound CMS payload, and avoids the Windows no-flag-font rendering issue.

* Separator is a middle dot ( · ) inside the market segment and a hyphen ( - ) between segments, so the market reads as one unit.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

1\. Both formulas pass Check Syntax and report compiled size under 15,000 characters.

2\. A Deal with no Partner renders no double separator and no orphaned space.

3\. A Deal with Market Country set and Market State blank renders "US · Multi-state".

4\. A Deal with Market Country blank renders Operator - Vertical only.

5\. Deal\__c hyperlink navigates to the Deal record in the same tab and its label text matches Deal_Name_\_c exactly.

6\. Deal list views (BUILD-119) and the Deal record page (BUILD-120) reflect the new label.

=== OPEN QUESTION ===

Deal_Name\__c and Deal_\_c now render identical strings - one as plain text, one as a hyperlink. Two adjacent columns showing the same text will read as a duplicate to reps. Decide before BUILD-119/BUILD-120 lock the layouts whether to keep both (HYPERLINK fields export as raw HTML and do not sort cleanly, which is the usual reason to keep a plain-text twin) or retire one.

comments.body:
Added some fields based on this mock up

[https://deal-management.netlify.app/deal-record.html](https://deal-management.netlify.app/deal-record.html)
[Test Data](https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Links__c/a0FWJ000004k91B2AQ/view?ws=%2Flightning%2Fr%2FDeal__c%2Fa00WJ00000XjC76YAF%2Fview)

**⚠️ Review risk: this was built against a link↔rep cardinality that is still contradictory across three calls.**

* **Jul 28, Joyce:** all links sit at deal level, CMS picks from a dropdown — implicitly **one-to-many**.

* **Aug 4, Emily \[14:45\]:** "Typically like a rep for a deal wouldn't have more than one link… it would be managed on Salesforce" — then \[16:12\]: "they can, in their lifetime, have, like, one-to-one. there's a potential for them to switch to a different link on the same deal."

* **Aug 4, Joyce \[15:43\]:** "I think what you're saying is, like, we just do one-to-one" — after acknowledging she changed the mock-up at the offsite without discussion.

* But Emily also confirmed there **will** be rep sharing / multiple reps on one link — which contradicts one-to-one.

The attached Deal mockup shows a Links related list with a **Reps count column** (4, 2, 0) and a **Default** flag — i.e. many reps per link, with one default. That is a third model again.

**Before accepting this review, pin down:** (a) can one link serve multiple reps simultaneously? (b) can one rep hold multiple active links on the same deal? (c) what does the Default flag actually govern?

Also noted Jul 28: there is **no Salesforce-side guardrail** that a link belongs to only one rep — that has to be enforced in the CMS. If (a) is "no", we are relying on a system we do not control to protect our data model. Worth pushing back on.
